\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\textbf{Subject-driven image generation.} Identity preservation in images has moved from per-subject optimization \cite{ruiz2023dreambooth, gal2022textual} and encoder-based adapters \cite{ye2023ipadapter, li2023blipdiffusion} to treating the reference as extra tokens of a diffusion transformer \cite{tan2024ominicontrol, xiao2024omnigen, wu2025uno}. The token-based formulation scales to large paired datasets whose references deliberately differ from their targets. We inherit this data regime and apply it to a video backbone.

\textbf{Subject-to-video generation.} Early identity-preserving video methods focus on faces \cite{he2024idanimator, yuan2024consisid}. Open-domain S2V methods condition a video backbone on arbitrary subjects by concatenating reference latents \cite{liu2025phantom, fei2025skyreelsa2}, through a unified conditioning interface \cite{jiang2025vace}, with multi-modal identity encoders \cite{hu2025hunyuancustom, deng2025magref}, or with a lightweight reference branch inside the backbone's self-attention \cite{xue2025standin}. All of them are trained on reference--video pairs, and OpenS2V-Nexus \cite{yuan2025opens2v} and MuSS \cite{muss2025} report the resulting copy-paste tendency. We reuse the reference branch of Stand-In \cite{xue2025standin}, but train it from images and add the two mechanisms that keep motion intact.

\textbf{Customizing video models from images.} AnimateDiff \cite{guo2023animatediff} attaches a separately trained motion module to customized image models. Closest to our Stage I, Still-Moving \cite{chefer2024stillmoving} trains a motion adapter on frozen videos to absorb the static bias of image training and removes it at inference. We differ in three ways: the adapter is trained with signed targets and becomes a continuous control rather than an on/off switch; it acts on a DiT with joint spatiotemporal attention; and instead of adapting the backbone, we keep it frozen and use the adapter as a fixed carrier for a separate appearance branch.

\textbf{Conditioning and guidance.} Classifier-free guidance \cite{ho2022cfg} and its multi-condition variants \cite{brooks2023instructpix2pix} contrast conditional and unconditional predictions; autoguidance \cite{karras2024autoguidance} contrasts a model with a weaker version of itself. In our readout the learned null reference is part of the training forward pass, not only an inference-time contrast.
